key_insight: A PEDOT:PSS/graphene/n-Si trilayer combines interfacial charge optimization with graphene’s protective barrier effect to deliver both higher efficiency and much better stability than single-layer Schottky junction cells.
engineering_relevance: The work suggests a practical, low-cost hybrid contact strategy for silicon photovoltaics where one functional layer improves optoelectronics while another suppresses ambient degradation.
method: Built a planar PEDOT:PSS/Gr/n-Si Schottky junction and compared it with Gr/n-Si and PEDOT:PSS/n-Si controls
Used the PEDOT:PSS layer as an anti-reflection coating, p-type dopant for graphene, and conductivity enhancer
Benchmarked performance and 75-day ambient stability on untextured silicon substrates
evidence_signal: The trilayer device reached 8.52% PCE versus 4.56% for pristine Gr/n-Si, and retained about 90% of its initial efficiency after 75 days, while PEDOT:PSS/n-Si retained only ~29%.
watch_item: The reported gains are demonstrated on untextured planar substrates, so real-device scaling and texture-compatible integration may change the performance benefit.
paper_title: Synergistic Graphene and PEDOT:PSS Layers on Silicon for Enhanced Efficiency and Stability in Schottky Junction Solar Cells
